reasons: The values are typed into the code rather than loaded from saved settings, so the page does not reflect real changes.
Personal contact details are stored in plain text in this file.

terms.meaning: A reusable piece of a web page, such as a header, that is written once and drawn wherever needed.
Written directly into the code instead of being loaded from storage or a server.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the shared header and footer so this page matches the rest of the app. Nothing is shown from this section by itself.
sections.why: Lets the page reuse the same top and bottom bars as the other pages.

sections.name: buckets
sections.title: Target job groups data
sections.what: A fixed list of four target job groups. Each has a name, job titles, seniority, locations, sectors and a number of applications. These become the cards in the last part of the page.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely placeholder data until saved settings exist.
sections.watch_out: Changing these values changes only this page. Nothing here saves them, so the rest of the app does not see the change.

sections.name: profile
sections.title: Personal profile data written in code
sections.what: Holds the name, contact details, location and web links shown in the Profile card.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely placeholder data entered directly in the file.
sections.watch_out: This file holds personal contact details in plain text. Anyone who can read or share the code can read them.

sections.name: portals
sections.title: Job portal list written in code
sections.what: Lists four job sites, each with an address, a status and a last scan date. The data is fixed text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely placeholder data for a real scan status.
sections.watch_out: The page does not scan any site, so the scan dates shown are not real results.

sections.name: ConfigPage (part 1)
sections.title: Profile and job portal cards
sections.what: Builds the page frame with the header and footer. Shows a Profile card that lists each profile field with its label in capitals, and a Job Portals card listing each site with its last scan date and a status tag. Ends with the heading for the target role section.
sections.why: Shows the setup at a glance on one page.
sections.watch_out: The Profile card shows every field in the profile data, so any field added there appears on the page automatically.

sections.name: ConfigPage (part 2)
sections.title: Target role bucket cards
sections.what: Shows each target job group as a card with its application count and four lines: titles, seniority, location and sectors.
sections.why: Lets the user see their targeting at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The four lines read fixed field names from each group. If a field is renamed in the data, its line shows blank text with no error.

summary: A read-only Configuration page that shows the user's profile, job portals and target job groups, all written directly in the code rather than loaded or saved.
purpose: Lets the user see their setup in one place. It does not let them change anything.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The data looks like placeholder values, so the page is probably a preview of a settings screen that is not finished.
how: The page first draws the shared header. Then it shows a Profile card built from the fixed profile data and a Job Portals card built from the fixed portal list, where an active site shows a green tag and any other status shows a grey tag. Last, it shows the target role buckets as cards built from the fixed bucket list. No data is fetched or saved in this file.
inputs: None from the user. The only inputs are the fixed lists written at the top of the file.
outputs: A configuration screen with three parts: Profile, Job Portals, and Target Role Buckets, each showing the fixed values.
risks: Personal contact details are written in plain text in this file. The job portal scan dates are fixed text, so the page looks like it scans sites when it does not. Changing values here changes only this page.
debug: If the page shows wrong or old values, check the fixed lists at the top of config/page.tsx. If the layout looks broken, check the shared styles in app/globals.css and the header and footer in app/components.tsx. This page makes no network requests, so network problems are not the cause.
